# llms.txt and LLM-readable documentation

> A markdown file — `/llms.txt` at a site root or at any subpath — that gives a language model a curated, priority-ordered map of a site's LLM-friendly content: an H1, a blockquote summary, optional prose, then H2 sections of `- [name](url): description` links. This index is for agents and people building, generating or consuming llms.txt and LLM-readable documentation: 170 source-anchored facts from 79 sources, filed under 6 concepts; skill document-formats.

## llms-full.txt page grammars

- [Facts: llms-full.txt page grammars](llms-facts.txt#llms-full-txt-page-grammars): 16 source-anchored facts from 11 sources
- [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org/): The links should point at clean markdown (a `.md` twin of each page) (2 facts)
- [llmstxt.org/intro.html](https://llmstxt.org/intro.html): Parser reference (core.py): header `^#\s*{title}\n+{summ}\n+{info}`; sections on `^##\s*(.*?$)`; links `-\s*\[{title}\]\({url}\){desc}`. (2 facts)
- [wislr.com/articles/ai-bot-behavior-log-analysis](https://www.wislr.com/articles/ai-bot-behavior-log-analysis/): `sitemap.xml` — Job: exhaustive inventory; no `.md` versions, no external links; Do AI bots fetch it?: yes (ClaudeBot, GPTBot, Bingbot) (1 fact)

- [Facts: llms.txt generation tooling](llms-facts.txt#llms-txt-generation-tooling): 46 source-anchored facts from 35 sources
- [mintlify.com/docs/ai](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/ai/llmstxt): Mintlify — Emits: llms.txt, llms-full.txt, `.md` per page, `/.well-known/` copies, `/_llms/` split indexes; Descriptions from: frontmatter `description` (truncated at 300 chars) (7 facts)
- [honeybound.co/blog/shopify-llms-txt-agents-md](https://honeybound.co/blog/shopify-llms-txt-agents-md): Shopify (Apr–May 2026, silent) — Emits: auto `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, `/agents.md`, `/sitemap_agentic_discovery.xml`, `/.well-known/ucp` — Liquid storefronts only (headless Hydrogen/Oxygen get `/.well-known/ucp` alone); Descriptions: boilerplate (2 facts)
- [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org/): `## Optional`. v1 gave it mechanical meaning ("the URLs provided there can be skipped if a shorter context is needed") (1 fact)

## llms.txt recreation and family aggregation

- [Facts: llms.txt recreation and family aggregation](llms-facts.txt#llms-txt-recreation-and-family-aggregation): 39 source-anchored facts from 19 sources
- [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org/): Structure (spec v2): H1 = product name; blockquote = one-paragraph summary; optional prose "how to interpret the files"; H2 sections (11 facts)
- [blog.cloudflare.com/content-signals-policy](https://blog.cloudflare.com/content-signals-policy/): Read `robots.txt` first (full mechanics: `references/robots-txt.md`; the Content Signals layer, including the `content-use` fourth signal Cloudflare is testing: `references/robots-txt-content-signals.md`): the sitemap pointer, disallow rules (3 facts)
- [gitdoc.ai/blog/llms-txt-ai-readable-documentation](https://gitdoc.ai/blog/llms-txt-ai-readable-documentation): 10–50 links for a product index; 4–7 sections; descriptions of 10–20 words that say *what a reader finds there*, with exact tokens (3 facts)
- [github.com/AnswerDotAI/llms-txt](https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/llms-txt/blob/main/llms_txt/core.py): Parse: H1 → title; first blockquote → summary; everything before the first H2 → info; each H2 → section (2 facts)
- [llmstxt.site](https://llmstxt.site/): Publish token counts (or page counts) beside each link so a consumer can budget before fetching. (2 facts)
